subject: Psychology
central_question: How does experience produce relatively lasting changes through conditioning, observation, cognition, verbal organisation and practice?
in_scope_units: Nature and features of learning and distinction from temporary change or performance.
Operant conditioning, reinforcement, punishment, schedules and delay.
Differences between classical and operant conditioning.
Reinforcement, shaping, extinction, generalisation, discrimination and spontaneous recovery.
banned_topics: Detailed memory-system models and forgetting theories, which belong to Human Memory.
Detailed motivational theories beyond motivation as a facilitator of learning.

known_pitfalls.correction: Learning is a relatively permanent change produced by experience; fatigue, drugs and habituation are excluded.
Negative reinforcement increases avoidance or escape by removing an unpleasant event; punishment suppresses a response.

known_pitfalls.claim: Classical and operant conditioning condition the same responses.
known_pitfalls.correction: Classical conditioning concerns elicited reflexes; operant conditioning concerns voluntary actions shaped by consequences.
Models transmit behaviour, while consequences affect performance.
It can occur with average or superior intelligence and adequate opportunity.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Review Question 1 on definition and features.
NCERT Review Question 2 on classical conditioning.
NCERT Review Question 3 on operant conditioning.
NCERT Review Question 10 on cognitive learning.
NCERT Review Question 11 on learning disabilities.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Review Questions 1–11 and one Project Idea.
